analysis:
Examined all five supplied batch analyses and all replayed metadata, patches and source. Independently visible changes add Waitlist command registration (provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/Darkbloom.swift:60), sandbox waitlist help (provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/Sandbox/SandboxCommand.swift:28-31), and account-level onboarding documentation (changelog.d/feature-waitlists.md:3-7). These establish new authenticated coordinator interaction and setup gating, but do not demonstrate a concrete credential leak, authorization bypass or unsafe execution path. Existing/local setup exemptions and compatibility with coordinators lacking waitlists are explicit policy choices, not proof of a serving-authorization regression. TB-002/TB-011 distinguish onboarding and registration from live serving permission; no supplied change establishes replacement of those controls.
The analyses collectively cover CLI documentation, cluster gate placement and sandbox test-fixture approval injection. Their implementation conclusions cannot all be independently verified: replay omits 13 of 21 reviewed units and contains neither the cluster gate nor production waitlist/sandbox flow implementations. No finding is supported solely by those analyses. No visible change affects inference encryption, cache isolation, Apple evidence, billing or privileged GPU/fan operations.
Material follow-up remains: inspect FeatureWaitlistClient/FeatureWaitlistAccess for token destination binding, redirects, bounded responses/timeouts and safe feature paths (A-008/A-018); FeatureWaitlistView for terminal sanitization; Cluster.Setup.requireNewPairApproval and pairing-state exemptions; and SandboxSetupFlow.requireApproval for refusal before installer execution or ownership side effects (TB-013/T-061/A-019). Verify pending, revoked and error tests separately from the reported approved fixtures. These are unresolved contracts in the new flow, not observed missing controls. The available evidence does not justify a vulnerability finding or a claim that the entire PR is safe.
